record.paper_title: Localized Spot Patterns on the Sphere for Reaction-Diffusion Systems: Theory and Open Problems
record.context_brief: DAE spot dynamics on varying-curvature manifolds
record.original_question: On a compact surface of revolution for which the source-neutral Green function is analytically available, with that Green function satisfying Delta_S G = |Omega|^{-1} - delta(x - x_0), can one derive and analyze explicit differential-algebraic spot dynamics for localized reaction-diffusion spots on a manifold with varying curvature, including whether curvature can pin localized spots?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a smooth compact two-dimensional surface of revolution embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with induced metric, surface area $|\Omega|$, Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta_{\mathcal{S}}$, and Gaussian curvature $K(x)$ that varies along $\mathcal{S}$. Assume that the source-neutral Green's function $G(x;x_0)$ on $\mathcal{S}$, defined by
$$\Delta_{\mathcal{S}} G(x;x_0) = \tfrac{1}{|\Omega|} - \delta(x-x_0), \qquad \int_{\mathcal{S}} G(x;x_0)\,dS = 0,$$
is available in closed analytic form (e.g. by separation of variables in geodesic polar coordinates adapted to the rotational symmetry).

Consider a singularly perturbed activator–inhibitor reaction–diffusion system on $\mathcal{S}$ (for instance, a Schnakenberg- or Gierer–Meinhardt-type model with small activator diffusivity $\varepsilon^2 \ll 1$) admitting quasi-equilibrium localized spot solutions concentrated at points $x_1(t),\ldots,x_N(t) \in \mathcal{S}$ with slowly varying source strengths $S_1(t),\ldots,S_N(t)$.

(a) Derive, by matched asymptotic expansions in the limit $\varepsilon \to 0$, an explicit differential-algebraic system of equations (DAE) governing the slow evolution of the spot locations $\{x_j(t)\}$ and source strengths $\{S_j(t)\}$ on $\mathcal{S}$, in which $G$ and its regular part $R(x_0) := \lim_{x\to x_0}(G(x;x_0)+\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\log d(x,x_0))$ enter as the only geometric data.

(b) Using the explicit form of $G$ on the surface of revolution, analyze the resulting DAE: characterize equilibrium spot configurations, their linear stability under slow translational perturbations, and determine whether the spatial variation of the Gaussian curvature $K$ can pin one or more spots at specific locations of $\mathcal{S}$ (i.e. produce isolated stable equilibria of the DAE that depend on $K$ rather than only on inter-spot interactions).
artifact.category_tag: localized spot dynamics on curved surfaces
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open direction: deriving and analyzing explicit DAE spot dynamics on general surfaces of revolution with varying curvature, and establishing curvature-induced pinning, has been treated rigorously only on the sphere (constant curvature). Subsequent works on curved-surface reaction-diffusion (e.g. weakly nonlinear analyses, curvature-dependent diffusion of Turing patterns, Turing pattern dynamics on curved surfaces in 2024–2025) study related phenomena but do not provide the explicit DAE reduction and pinning analysis requested here. No definitive resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: The dynamics of localized spot patterns for reaction-diffusion systems on the sphere
status_evidence.snippet: DAE system of ODEs for the locations of a collection of spots on the sphere is derived; varying-curvature case left as future work.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous DAE spot dynamics established for the sphere (constant curvature).

status_evidence.title: Weakly nonlinear analysis of Turing pattern dynamics on curved surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Amplitude equations for reaction-diffusion equations on curved surfaces are derived.
status_evidence.claim: Related curved-surface analyses exist but do not provide the explicit spot DAE and pinning analysis on surfaces of revolution.

status_evidence.title: Oscillatory and chaotic pattern dynamics driven by surface curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Curvature drives nontrivial pattern dynamics on curved surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Curvature effects on patterns are an active research area, but the specific DAE pinning question remains unresolved.
